note: Adapted from the species-level description of Emerson (1928), originally in English; only the soldier is described, the worker and the alate are not recorded; the description is based on 2 soldiers (in the same vial as Mirotermes (Cubitermes) antennalis); “tHe fourth” in the original is an OCR corruption; synonymy, figure numbers and localities are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very close to M. mirandus, differing in the shape of the pronotum and of the mandibles: in M. mirandus the labrum is proportionally shorter with a deeper incision, and the mandibles are bent at about two-thirds of their length from the base and are straighter, whereas in this species the mandibles are bent at the middle; the outer half of the inner margin of the mandibles is straighter in this species than in either M. mandibularis or M. mirandus.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale yellow, oblong; the sides straight and parallel; posterior margin slightly rounded; anterior surface vertical. Antennae 14- or 15-segmented; with 14 segments, segments 2 and 3 are about equal in length and segment 4 is shorter than segment 3; with 15 segments, segment 3 is slightly shorter than segment 4 and segment 4 is shorter than segment 2. Labrum bilobed, the sides straight and parallel. Mandibles long, bent outward at the middle; the apex incurved, each mandible with a small tooth on the inner margin halfway from the base to the bend. The tip of the nasus blunt, surrounded by short setae, similar to Cubitermes s. str. The sides of the pronotum straight, markedly narrowed posteriorly; posterior margin slightly notched. Abdominal tergites covered with short hairs, the posterior margins with longer setae; sternites with long hairs. Measurements (mm): total length 6.00–7.00, head length including the mandibles 4.00, head length to the clypeal margin 2.30, head width 1.44, antennal length 2.44, pronotal width 0.89, hind tibia length 1.00, left mandible length 2.40–2.50.
